DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA comer Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http://wvw-/.dilq.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 82 s. 2021 22 June 2021 ATTY. ANTHONY C. NUYDA, CESO Ill Regional Director, Region V Rizal St., Legazpi City Dear Dir. Nuyda: This in reference to your Memorandum dated 01 March 2021 seeking this Department's guidance relative to Provincial Ordinance No. 16-2019. Contextually, on 26 September 2019, the Sangguniang Panlungsod of Sorsogon issued Provincial Ordinance No. 16-2019, entitled "An Ordinance Providing for the Representation of Members of the Sangguniang Barangay in the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Sorsogon, to Directly and Fully Participate in Local Governance Through Policy-Making and for Other Purposes" It is the duly acknowledged by your Office, that while the subject ordinance enjoys the presumption of validity unless otherwise declared by a court of justice, it is deemed appropriate to elevate the issue for this Department's opinion. Further, it is the posited that Sectoral Representation in sanggunian is confined to those provided in Section 41(c) of the LGC, as reiterated in Section 467(b) and (c) of the same law. Thus, the creation of an ordinance providing for representation of the sanggunian barangay kagawad in the sangguniang panlalawigan not only amended the Local Government Code but also created confusion. Hence, the foregoing, as the action of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Sorsogon may take precedent among other local government units.

At the outset, it may be well to stress that Provincial Ordinance No. 16-2019 dated 26 September 2019, was already adopted by the Sangguniang Panlungsod of Sorsogon. An ordinance that has undergone the procedural process for its enactment under the Local Government Code is presumed valid unless declared otherwise by our courts of justice. However, this rule must be exercised with caution. Distinction must be made between ordinances which are glaringly violative of the Constitution or existing laws and those which are not. In relation thereto, may we invite your attention to Section 41(b) and (c) of Republic Act No. 7160, otherwise known as the "Local Government Code of 1991", in relation to Section 457 of the same Code, which provides: SECTION 41. Manner of Election. xxx (b) The regular members of the sangguniang panlalawigan, sangguniang panlungsod, and sangguniang bayan shall be elected by district as follows: First and second-class provinces shall have ten (IO) regular members; third and foutth-class provinces, eight (8); and fifth and sixth-class provinces, six (6): Provided, That in provinces having more than five (5) legislative districts, each district shall have two (2) sangguniang panlalawigan members, without prejudice to the provisions of Section 2 of Republic Act No. 6637. Sangguniang barangay members shall be elected at large. The presidents of the leagues of sanggunian members of component cities and municipalities shall serve as ex officio members of the sangguniang panlalawigan concerned. The presidents of the liga ng mga barangay and the pederasyon ng mga sangguniang kabataan elected by their respective chapters, as provided in this Code, shall serve as ex officio members of the sangguniang panlalawigan, sangguniang panlungsod, and sangguniang bayan. (c) In addition thereto, there shall be one (I) sectoral representative from the women, one (I) from the workers, and one (I) from any of the following sectors: the urban poor, indigenous cultural communities, disabled persons, or any other sector as may be determined by the sanggunian concerned within ninety (90) days prior to the holding of the next local elections as may be provided for by law. The COMELEC shall promulgate the rules and regulations to effectively provide for the election of such sectoral representatives. (Emphasis Supplied)

SECTION 457. Composition - (a) The sangguniang panlungsod, the legislative body of the city, shall be composed of the city vice-mayor as presiding officer, the regular sanggunian members, the president of the city chapter of the liga ng mga barangay, the president of the panlungsod na pederasyon ng mga sangguniang kabataan, and the sectoral representatives, as members. (b) In addition thereto, there shall be three (3) sectoral representatives: one (1) from the women; and as shall be determined by the sanggunian concerned within ninety (90) days prior to the holding of the local elections, one (1) from the agricultural or industrial workers; and one (I) from the other sectors, including the urban poor, indigenous cultural communities, or disabled persons. (c) The regular members of the sangguniang panlungsod and the sectoral representatives shall be elected in the manner as may be provided for by law. Clearly, based from the foregoing, the members of the Sagguniang Panlalawigan are composed only of: (1) city vice mayor as the presiding office, (2) regular sangguniang members which were elected by district, (3) president of the city chapter of the liga ng mga barangay, (4) president of the panlungsod na pederasyon ng mga sangguniang kabataan, and (5) sectoral representatives. In addition, there shall be three (3) sectoral representatives as provided in Section 457 of the LGC, which has been elaborately explained in DILG Legal Opinion No. 14, Series of 20141. In gist, the said legal opinion provides emphasis on sectoral representation in the sanggunian, and noted the fact that, except for indigenous representatives, Congress has yet to pass a law providing for the manner of electing the other sectoral representatives in the Sangguniang Panlungsod. (Emphasis and Underscoring Supplied) At this juncture, it bears emphasis that based on the aforementioned provisions of the law, there is no mention of representation by the duly elected President of the Pederasyon ng Sangguniang Barangay Kagawads as ex-officio member of the Sangguniang Panlungsod and/or member of the 1 Dated 22 April 2014

local boards, for that matter. Further, Section 457 of the Code mandates that the sectoral representatives shall be elected in the manner provided for by law. Hence, we hereby concur to the position of DILG Region V. Accordingly, may we remind the sanggunian concerned that for an ordinance to be valid in substance, it (1) must not contravene the Constitution or any statute; (2) must not be unfair or oppressive; (3) must not be partial or discriminatory; (4) must not prohibit, but may regulate trade; (5) must be general and consistent with public policy; and (6) must not be unreasonable2. Based on the foregoing, the subject ordinance, on its face, violates Republic Act No. 7160, otherwise known as the "Local Government Code", as discussed above. Accordingly, this Department accedes to your position that the creation of an ordinance providing for representation of the sanggunian barangay kagawad in the sangguniang panlalawigan not only amended the Local Government Code but also created confusion. This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have assisted you accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: INGAN Unders retary for Local Government LegalÆ 1 Copy Furnished. Atty.
